entries.summary: Shell dtypes (float4_e2m1fn_x2, the bits types and the sub-byte integers) have no value conversions, and copy_ rejects casts to or from them via check_shell_dtype_cast. Elementwise ops that mix a shell dtype with…
entries.text: Shell dtypes (float4_e2m1fn_x2, the bits types and the sub-byte integers) have no value conversions, and copy_ rejects casts to or from them via check_shell_dtype_cast. Elementwise ops that mix a shell dtype with another dtype were only rejected on CPU, as a side effect of TensorIterator creating the promotion temporaries through copy_. Other devices convert inside their kernels: on CUDA, x_fp4 == True compared the scalar's bits against the packed float4 bytes, and comparing against a 0-dim uint8 or float8 tensor hit the device-side assert in DynamicCast.h, which poisons the CUDA context. TensorIterator::compute_types now calls check_shell_dtype_cast whenever it converts an input to the common dtype or the common dtype to an output of a different dtype, on every device including meta, so every backend raises the same NotImplementedError as CPU. The check costs a dtype comparison only when operand dtypes differ. check_shell_dtype_cast moves from an anonymous namespace in Copy.cpp to ATen/native/Copy.h so TensorIterator, and kernels that convert without TensorIterator, can call it. Test Plan: python test/test_type_promotion.py python test/quantization/core/experimental/test_floatx.py python test/test_binary_ufuncs.py -k "eq or ne or comparison" test_shell_dtype_promotion_raises checks eq/ne of a float4 tensor against a bool, an int, a float and a 0-dim uint8 tensor, and an add into a float4 out=, on every device test_type_promotion runs on (CPU, CUDA, XPU). entries.summary: ✴️ iz2: Rebasing or merging changes the files in the workspace. With this change, the mergebot workflows (trymerge.yml, tryrebase.yml, revert.yml) copy .github/scripts right after they check out main, and every helper…
entries.text: ✴️ iz2: Rebasing or merging changes the files in the workspace. With this change, the mergebot workflows (trymerge.yml, tryrebase.yml, revert.yml) copy .github/scripts right after they check out main, and every helper runs from that copy. GIT_REPO_DIR is set to the workspace, so git operations still target it. Without it, gitutils.get_git_repo_dir() would resolve the repo from the copy's own path. trymerge.py writes merge_record.json relative to its own file, so the S3 upload now reads it from ${{ runner.temp }}/mergebot/. "Comment on Canceled" now runs only if the staging step finished, because the helper it calls lives in the copy. test_mergebot_status.py lists the reviewed steps of trymerge.yml and revert.yml; it now has the new staging step and the staged script paths. Replies still go only through trymerge.py and comment_on_pr.py. Test plan: ran the patched steps in a test repo with the scripts at 55da759. tryrebase.py --dry-run ran from the copy against a live PR, and its git commands ran in the workspace. In every invocation the helpers loaded their modules from the copy only. merge_record.json landed where the upload step reads it, and upload-artifact-s3 found the file. A cancel after staging ran the comment step; a cancel before staging skipped it. test_mergebot_status.py passes, and fails against the unpatched trymerge.yml and revert.yml. lintrunner is clean on the changed files. Pull Request resolved: #205960 Approved by: https://github.com/huydhn

entries.text: Part of #192126. Adds the eight bytearray predicate methods to ByteArrayVariable: isalnum(), isalpha(), isascii(), isdigit(), islower(), isspace(), istitle() and isupper(). They are registered in tp_methods and reuse the existing _bytearray_case_method helper (the same METH_NOARGS pattern as upper/lower/title). The arity check in Method raises CPython's TypeError for calls like b.isalpha(1) or b.isalnum(x=1). The handlers and table entries sit after expandtabs, so they don't overlap #205394 (capitalize/swapcase). Changes torch/_dynamo/variables/lists.py: add bytearray_isalnum … bytearray_isupper. test/dynamo/test_bytearray.py: add test_isalnum, test_isalpha, test_isascii, test_isdigit, test_islower, test_isspace, test_istitle, test_isupper. They cover true and false cases, an empty bytearray (True only for isascii), non-ASCII bytes, and the exact TypeError message for a positional argument (plus a keyword argument for isalnum). Also add test_input_bytearray_is_methods, which uses torch.compile(fullgraph=True) with bytearray inputs and checks the input is unchanged, and test_bytearray_is_methods_after_mutation, which checks that results reflect a slice store made inside the compiled function. Delete eight expected-failure markers: CPython313-test_bytes-ByteArrayAsStringTest.test_{isalnum,isalpha,isascii,isdigit,islower,isspace,istitle,isupper}. Testing Run on a torch 2.16.0.dev20261119 CPU nightly with torch/_dynamo/variables/lists.py taken from this branch (base efbc870), Pyt
